display.text:
# Context Pack: `sprint-execute-resume` — Sprint execute queue and resume Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen, clean tree). Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5. Domain: governed-sprint-delivery. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments. ## 1. Purpose Executes the top-level task checkboxes of a validated `plan.md` through a reusable agent session, with product-owned durability around every agent turn: - **Queue execution**: one ordered pass over plan tasks; first turn gets shared sprint context + full queue; later turns are compact continuations in the same session when a reusable session ID exists (fallback: independent full prompts). - **Persist-before-launch checkpointing**: each task is persisted as `running` before the runtime call, and its terminal outcome is persisted before the next task starts; session IDs observed mid-stream are also checkpointed. - **Stop-on-failure discipline**: queue halts on the first failed or cancelled task. - **Stale-running reconcile**: `running` records left by dead owners become `failed` with diagnostics at three distinct points (startup recovery, resume reconciliation, pre-execution check). - **Deferral protocol**: CLI `--defer --reason` (operator) or an agent-authored plan marker `- [/] Task N: ... — Deferred: ` (agent); both require rationale and produce durable `deferred` outcomes; the plan checkbox stays visibly unchecked. - **Resume validation**: `--resume` allows checked/deferred plan markers only when the run state already records matching terminal outcomes per stable task ID. - **Containment**: the agent's working directory is set to the resolved approved target (worktree preferred), with in-prompt safety constraints forbidding git mutation and out-of-scope artifacts. - **Publication**: when every task resolves (complete|deferred), git publication commits the implementation worktree (`All=true`) then the workspace artifacts (`execute.md`, `.run-state.json`), config-gated. Primary code: `internal/sprint/execute.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_state.go`, `execute_target.go`, `execute_model.go`, plus `internal/sprint/publication.go:57-78` and `internal/app/git_publication.go`. ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow ### CLI dispatch (`internal/app/sprint_commands.go:329-368`) - Flag parsing `parseSprintExecuteArgs` (1193-1233): `--task `, `--dry-run|--prompt`, `--resume`, `--defer --reason `, `--model `. Constraints: `--defer` requires `--task`; `--defer` cannot combine with `--dry-run`, `--resume`, or `--model`. Unknown flags → ExitUsage. - Non-dry-run, non-defer runs are wrapped as durable operations: `beginDurableCLICommand(OperationExecuteStart, ...Task: req.TaskID)` (durable_operations.go:49-138 — run-control acceptance, owner claim with lease+fencing, running lifecycle event, heartbeat/cancel-watch goroutine). The command context becomes cancellation-aware. Service is rebuilt via `sprintRuntimeService` (685-711) with the real runtime, publisher (`stagePublisher`: nil publisher when `git.stage_completion=off`), stage runtime models, QA/smoke settings. - Deferral runs `DeferExecuteTask` on the plain (non-runtime) service against `deps.ctx`; no durable wrapper. - Error classification after render: findings present → ExitValidation; error contains "failed tasks" → ExitPartial; contains "runtime" → ExitRuntime; otherwise `mapSprintError`. - Output rendering `renderSprintExecute` (1372-1402): project/sprint, dry-run prompt dump, result message, run-state/summary paths, per-task `id status attempts=N` lines, findings list. Help text at 1530-1531, 1571-1580. ### Web / TUI / flow entrypoints - Web operation spec `"execute"|"execute-start"` maps to `OperationExecuteStatus | OperationExecuteDryRun | OperationExecuteResume | OperationExecuteStart` based on options (`internal/web/operation_handlers.go:646-666`). TUI exposes Execute Status/Dry Run/Start/Resume nav items (`internal/tui/model.go:480-483`). - `internal/app/operation_runner.go:53-58`: execute-start/resume → `service.Execute(ctx, p, s, ExecuteRequest{TaskID, ModelOverride, Resume: kind==OperationExecuteResume})`; dry-run variant at `operations.go:443`. - Flow integration (`internal/sprint/flow.go`): execute is the 8th cumulative stage; `runFlowStage` case StageExecute → `s.Execute(ctx, ..., ExecuteRequest{DryRun: req.DryRun, Resume: true})` (flow.go:241) — flow always resumes. Flow skips its generic planning-stage publication for execute (execute publishes itself, flow.go:142-155, 167) and uses `ExecuteComplete` for the skip check (flow.go:307-308 → verify.go:134-140). ### `Service.Execute` main loop (`internal/sprint/execute.go:129-349`) 1. Acquire mutation lock unless DryRun (`acquireMutationContext`, locks.go:112-126 — cross-process file lease shared by flow/execute/review/smoke/verify; reentrant via context marker). 2. `prepareExecute` (351-384): resolve sprint inputs → `planManifest` → `resolveSprintTarget(create=false)` → read plan artifact → `extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, allowChecked=req.Resume)` → if Resume, `validateResolvedResumeTasks` → TaskID existence check → `executeModelSelection(override)` (override > planning.execute_model > planning.plan_model > runtime provider/model; unresolved model ⇒ finding). Any finding aborts before any write ("execute prerequisites failed validation"). 3. Read planning inputs; `prepareSharedPromptContext(..., persistCache=true)` — code-context-derived shared prefix, cached context pack, fails closed when code-context exists but is invalid (`prompt_context.go:93-123`). 4. DryRun: composes the first (or selected) task's prompt and returns; no state writes, no runtime. 5. Fresh vs resumed state: `records := ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks, now)`; `state := NewExecuteRunState(sp, target, planPath, PlanFingerprint(mustReadPlan), records, now)`. If `req.Resume` AND load succeeds → `state = reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now)` (existing records substituted by ID into planned order; stale `running` → `failed` with "recovered stale running task on resume"). Load errors on resume are ignored (fresh state wins). Then unconditional `SaveExecuteRunState`. 6. `executionQueue := executeQueueFromState(state.Tasks, tasks, req.TaskID)` — planned tasks whose record is not complete/deferred, optionally narrowed to one ID. 7. Session reuse gate (186-193): only when `req.Resume` and `state.Target.Path == target.Path`; picks the last filtered record whose Runtime.Model equals the first queued task's effective model and has a SessionID (`reusableExecuteSession`, 563-574). 8. Per-task loop over `state.Tasks` (skips others when TaskID set): - Skip `complete`; `running` → `failed` + "stale-running ... before resume" diagnostic; proceed only if now pending|failed|cancelled. - Mark running, `Attempts++`, StartedAt; persist — failure aborts before launch ("persist running execute task %q"). - Per-task model: inline plan annotation `` overrides batch selection (`executeSelectionForTask`, 739-744). - `continueSession := batchSessionID != "" && models match` → compact `RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt` with empty prefix and `SessionAction="continue"`; otherwise full `renderExecuteSessionPrompt` (RenderExecutePrompt + ordered queue section + direct-input packet: project definition inputs, sprint-index, technical-handbook, reasoning directory inputs, reasoning.md, plan.md). - Metadata: session_mode initial|continue|fresh-fallback, execution_turn, execution_queue_size, model_source, stage, task. - `runtimeRequest` (service.go:1122-1169): scoped runtime store owner/path under the sprint dir, PromptRef with sha256 checksum, trace ID, stable-prefix cache directive. `runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path` (execute.go:245). `OnEvent` wrapper checkpoints any new SessionID into run state under a mutex (save errors captured, surfaced post-run). - `startSprintRuntime` (runtime_metrics.go:116-125): `pruntime.CleanupRuntimeStores(sp.Path, 72h, 2GiB, false)` then `runtime.StartRun`; runtime metrics persisted separately (failure degrades to warning). - Post-run classification precedence (287-313): checkpoint save error → failed/"state-save-failed"; deferral read-back error → failed/"invalid-deferral"; deferral reason non-empty → deferred + rationale diagnostic; ctx cancelled → cancelled; runtime error → failed/"runtime-failed"; ≥1 artifact → complete + evidence entries (paths sanitized by `safeArtifactPath`); warning containing "diagnostic-only" → complete + "diagnostic-only-completion"; else failed/"missing-evidence". - Terminal state persisted ("persist terminal execute task"); checkpoint errors abort the whole command afterwards. Failed or cancelled breaks the loop; single-task mode always breaks. - On success, batchSessionID/batchSessionModel advance from the run result (or task.Runtime fallback). 9. `WriteExecuteSummary` → `projects/

/sprints//execute.md` (plain `os.WriteFile` 0644 inside contained path): counts per status, per-task attempts/evidence/diagnostics lines. 10. Any failed/cancelled ⇒ returns result plus error "execute completed with failed tasks". 11. Best-effort `_ = s.deleteCompletedSessions(...)` per runtime result (deletes session(s)/runtime store; flow.go:26-56). 12. If `allExecuteTasksResolved` (≥1 task, all complete|deferred) → `publishExecuteStage` (publication.go:57-78): implementation publish `{Root: target.Path, All: true}` then workspace publish of `execute.md` + `.run-state.json`; identical commit message "ultraplan: sprint

/ complete execute" with `UltraPlan-Publication:` identity trailer; skipped results filtered when publisher disabled. ### `DeferExecuteTask` (execute.go:29-79) Trims reason; requires non-empty taskID+reason, ≤1000 chars, no `\x00\r\n`. Mutation lock; loads state; rejects deferring complete/deferred tasks; marks deferred (+CompletedAt, "deferred" diagnostic with redacted reason); saves state and summary; unknown ID errors. Does not modify plan.md. ### Resume validation (`validateResolvedResumeTasks`, execute.go:386-421) When resuming and plan.md has `[x]` or `[/]` top-level markers: requires a loadable valid run state ("checked tasks lack execution state" otherwise); each resolved marker must map to matching status (`[x]`→complete, `[/]`→deferred) by task ID; mismatches become blocking findings. ### Target resolution (`ResolveExecuteTarget` / `resolveSprintTarget`, execute_target.go) - Extract `**Target Implementation Directory:**` (bold or plain bullet, backtick-trimmed) from project-index.md; absolute or workspace-root-relative; must stat to an existing directory. - If `.workspace.json` exists it wins (Source ".workspace.json"): validated against current source root (clean-path equality), worktree dir exists and is a dir, same git common dir as source, current branch equals recorded branch. Invalid → findings; unreadable/malformed → findings; absent + create=false → raw source target. - Worktree creation happens at the code-context stage (`create=true` in flow.go:138), not here: `createSprintWorkspace` requires the source be a clean git worktree root (no uncommitted changes), creates `ultraplan//` branch at HEAD under sibling `.basename-ultraplan-worktrees/` dir, writes `.workspace.json` atomically (rollback removes worktree+branch if the record write fails). ### Publication mechanics (`internal/platform/gitpublish/publisher.go`) Modes off|commit|commit-and-push. Resolves repo root + current branch (detached HEAD rejected), acquires `ultraplan-publish.lock` in the git common dir, builds a temporary index (`read-tree parent`, `add -A -- paths`, `write-tree`), skips commit when tree equals parent tree, else `commit-tree -p parent` + `update-ref commit parent` (CAS against concurrent branch movement) + index reconcile. Push honors upstream remote/ref, else pushes HEAD to configured remote with `--set-upstream`; `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, push timeout (default 2m). Path requests are containment-checked against the repo root. ## 3. Inputs / outputs Inputs: - argv flags; workspace root; cwd/env via workspace discovery. - `project-index.md` `Project Scope > Target Implementation Directory` line (agent-writable planning artifact; selects both the agent workdir and the wholesale-commit root). - `plan.md` content: top-level `- [ ] Task N: Name` checkboxes (bold-tolerant), nested `- [ ]` steps, `>` quote lines scanned for `Decision N` / `REQ-N-N` / `AC-N` refs, evidence heuristics (step text containing evidence/verification/test/check), `- [/]` deferral markers with `— Deferred:`/`- Deferred:` suffix reasons, inline `` annotations. Plan must pass `ValidatePlanContent` against the plan manifest first. - Planning inputs packet (requirements/code-context/sprint-index/handbook/reasoning dirs/reasoning.md/plan.md) rendered into the first-turn prompt. - `.run-state.json` or productstate DB record (schemaVersion 1) for resume/status; legacy schemaVersion-0 terminal files recognized read-only. - `.workspace.json` worktree record; config keys (`planning.execute_model`, `planning.plan_model`, `models.primary/default`, `git.stage_completion|remote|push_timeout`, runtime config); live agent runtime. Outputs: - Human stdout render; exit codes (0 ok / 2 usage / validation-class / partial for failed tasks / runtime-class). - Files written: `.run-state.json` (atomic temp+fsync+rename+dir-sync, JSON indent+newline), `execute.md` (plain truncate-write), runtime metrics file, disposable context-pack cache. - Git commits and optional pushes in two repos (implementation worktree, workspace) when all tasks resolved and publishing enabled. - Durable run-control events (accept/claim/lifecycle/heartbeat/terminal) for non-dry-run CLI executions. - Runtime side effects delegated to the agent: file edits inside WorkDir=target.Path, test execution, etc. ## 4. Authoritative state - **`.run-state.json` schemaVersion 1** (`domain.go:12,122-133`): header {schemaVersion, project, sprint, target{path,source}, planPath (contained relative), planFingerprint `sha256:` of whitespace-normalized lowercase plan text, createdAt, updatedAt} + ordered `tasks[]` {id `task-<12 hex>`, identity{name, planLine≥1, decisions[], requirements[], evidence[]}, status, attempts≥0, createdAt, updatedAt, startedAt?, completedAt?, diagnostics[], evidence[], runtime?}. - Statuses: pending / running / complete / deferred / failed / cancelled; terminal = complete|deferred|failed|cancelled (`domain.go:63-70`, execute_state.go:271-273). - **Validation contract** `ValidateExecuteRunState` (execute_state.go:184-268): strict schemaVersion==1; project/sprint identity match; safe contained planPath; fingerprint charset (no `\x00\r\n`); ≥1 task; unique IDs; safe identity text; deferred requires completedAt + a `deferred` diagnostic with non-blank rationale; running requires startedAt; terminal requires completedAt; diagnostics need code+message+time and safe charset; evidence needs kind+summary and optionally a safe relative path. - **Dual-home behavior**: when the productstate DB is enabled, the DB record is authoritative — `Save` writes DB first, then mirrors the file only once every task is terminal (checkpoint semantics, execute_state.go:105-130); `Load` prefers the DB record (state_database.go:38-55). Otherwise the file is primary. Migration hooks exist (`MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase`). - **Legacy compatibility**: schemaVersion-0 `{status: complete|failed|cancelled, files[], testsRun[], blockers[]}` files are historical evidence only (`LegacyTerminalExecuteStatus`), never resumable; `requireCompleteExecute` (verify.go:100-132) additionally accepts that legacy shape (status complete/completed with files[] plus non-empty execute.md) as completion evidence. - **`.workspace.json`** (`execute_target.go:16-27`): {schemaVersion:1, sourceRoot, path, branch, baseline, createdAt}; created at code-context stage; validated on every execute target resolution. - **`execute.md`**: derived human summary; plain WriteFile (not atomic); regenerated after every run/deferral. - **`plan.md`**: user-owned input; execute never writes it. The *agent* may edit markers during a turn; execute re-reads it after each turn (`agentDeferredTaskReason`, 423-450: full manifest + extraction revalidation, returning the marker reason only for the exact task). The recorded `PlanFingerprint` is captured once at state creation (via `mustReadPlan`, which swallows read errors) and is not re-verified later in the loop. - Note (descriptive): a resume attempt with unchecked plan tasks but an unreadable/malformed `.run-state.json` passes prepareExecute (no resolved markers ⇒ no findings; load error ignored at execute.go:177) and proceeds with fresh state, overwriting the prior file on first save. ## 5. Invariants (as implemented) - No runtime launch before the `running` transition is durably saved; no queue advance before the terminal outcome is saved; mid-stream session-ID events are also checkpointed. - Queue stops at the first failed or cancelled task; completed/deferred tasks are never re-executed within a run. - Resume reconciliation matches strictly by deterministic ID (normalized name+decisions+requirements+evidence hash); renamed/edited tasks get new IDs and their old records drop out of the reconciled list; deferral markers and model annotations deliberately do not change IDs (test-asserted). - Stale-running recovery exists in three layers: `ReconcileInterruptedMutation` (startup, code "recovery-interrupted"), `reconcileExecuteState` (resume), and the in-loop pre-execution check ("before resume"). - Deferral requires rationale at every layer: CLI flag validation, plan-marker regex requiring a reason, state-validation rationale diagnostic, and `invalid-deferral` classification when the read-back fails. - Completion gating: success requires ≥1 runtime artifact or an explicit "diagnostic-only" warning; otherwise failed/"missing-evidence". - Agent workdir is exactly the resolved target path (worktree preferred when valid); evidence paths stored in state must be safe relative paths or dropped. - Publication happens only when all tasks are terminal-resolved (complete|deferred); implementation repo commits before workspace artifacts; both silently skipped when publishing is off. - All persisted messages/diagnostics route through redaction/truncation helpers (`safeExecuteText` → `config.RedactValue`, ≤180 chars via `safeError`). - Session reuse additionally requires unchanged target path and equal effective model; otherwise fresh full prompts ("fresh-fallback"). ## 6. Trust boundaries - **plan.md as control input**: checkbox syntax, task names, decision/requirement references, deferral reasons, and `` annotations are parsed from an agent-writable artifact. The annotation string flows into runtime model selection without charset restriction beyond the annotation regex `[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]+`; marker deferral reasons are captured by regex without length limits at parse time (charset-checked later at state validation; redacted at persistence). - **project-index.md** decides which directory the agent may mutate and which repository gets committed wholesale (`All=true`) at publication. - **Agent output → durable state**: artifacts/warnings/session IDs from the runtime become state records; evidence URI must pass `safeRelPath` else stored empty; all free-text redacted. - **Agent constraints are prompt-level** (`ExecuteSafetyInstructions`, execute_target.go:220-227): stay inside approved target; do not create smoke/review/issues artifacts; do not run/request git mutation; no cross-sprint/TUI/hosted work. Technical enforcement of sandbox/permissions belongs to the opencode-agent-runtime surface (configured sandbox/permission policy travels on the runtime request). - **gitpublish** executes git with sanitized env (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, LC_ALL=C), validates remote names (no leading dash, restricted charset), and CAS-updates the branch ref. - **Mutation serialization**: cross-process sprint mutation lease (file lock) plus durable run-control owner fencing serialize execute against flow/review/smoke/verify and other owners. ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics - Mutates the implementation repo (through the delegated agent), can commit and push it, commits workspace artifacts, deletes completed sessions/runtime stores best-effort, prunes stale runtime stores (>72h, >2GiB). - **Cancellation**: durable-context cancel during a turn classifies the task cancelled (+diagnostic), breaks the queue, persists, returns result with error; run-control finish records cancelled. The in-flight runtime call receives the same ctx. - **Crash/restart**: orphaned `running` records recover to failed on startup reconcile or next resume; cleanup-uncertain marker forces explicit operator handling instead of silent reconcile (locks.go:40-44,101-108); legacy terminal states remain readable. - **Retry**: rerunning without `--resume` rebuilds fresh state (prior file replaced on first save); failed/cancelled/pending tasks restart with Attempts++; `--resume` keeps complete/deferred history and continues the remaining queue, reusing the session when target and model still match. - **Partial failure**: mixed-status state persisted, execute.md reflects counts, command exits ExitPartial-class with "execute completed with failed tasks". - Publication failure after full resolution surfaces as command error while leaving all tasks resolved and state saved (commit may exist without push; push timeout bounded). ## 8. Immediate surface dependencies - **sprint-planning-chain**: `resolveSprintInputs`, `planManifest`, `ValidatePlanContent`, plan artifact reads, direct-input packet composition, shared prompt prefix/context pack. - **sprint-flow-state**: flow dispatches execute (always Resume:true), skips its own publish step for execute, gates skip-checks via `ExecuteComplete`; execute itself does not write flow-state.json. - **opencode-agent-runtime** (`internal/platform/runtime`): Request/Result/Event contract — SessionID/SessionAction continuation, OnEvent stream, Artifacts/Warnings driving completion classification, RuntimeStore scoping/cleanup, usage/metrics summaries. - **repo-publication** (`internal/platform/gitpublish`): policy modes, repo lock, temp-index commit strategy, push semantics. - **product-state-mirror** (`internal/productstate`): authoritative DB record {header, items keyed by task ID with ordinals} behind `ExecuteStateInDatabase`. - **run-control / durable operations**: acceptance, claim, fencing, heartbeats, cancellation watch, terminal proposals wrapping every non-dry-run CLI execute. - **workspace scaffold**: embedded `prompts/execute-sprint.md` documents the superseded agent-authored execution mode (writes legacy schemaVersion-0-style `.run-state.json` itself); still materialisable via `defaults install`. ## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence) From target-repo `docs/cli-reference.md` (~L306-330, execute section): - One reusable agent session; first turn carries shared context + ordered queue; later tasks are compact continuations; UltraPlan checkpoints each task before advancing; stops on failure/cancellation; writes `.run-state.json` and `execute.md`; requires runtime evidence or a safe diagnostic before marking complete; constrains work to the project-index target; falls back to complete independent prompts when no reusable session ID is supplied. - Deferral: `--task --defer --reason ""` is durable and terminal, shown in execute.md and status counts; plan checkbox remains unchecked; review accepts deferrals only with a matching governed deferred outcome; arbitrary unchecked/manually checked tasks cannot bypass execution; `[/]` marker without `— Deferred: ` is invalid. From ultraplan-workspace sprint 23 (`projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/23-execute-stage/requirements.md` ~L22-49, L104): - Versioned, atomic, strictly-loaded, resumable `.run-state.json` recording statuses with attempts, timestamps, diagnostics, runtime metadata summaries; stale running tasks recovered to retryable-or-failed with diagnostics without redoing complete tasks; sprint status reflects execute readiness without runtime calls; execute.md cites plan.md and records counts/evidence/diagnostics; same-directory atomic writes; malformed/unsupported schemas rejected with actionable diagnostics. - Neutral divergence fact: sprint-23 enumerates five statuses (pending/running/complete/failed/cancelled); the implementation adds `deferred` as a sixth, documented instead in cli-reference.md. From ultraplan-workspace PRD (~L223, L576, L605): controlled execution from validated plan.md tasks is in scope; automatic Git-mutation *commands* and issue tracking remain deferred product non-goals (config-gated publication of completed work is implemented separately from the agent-side git ban). In-prompt contract (`ExecuteSafetyInstructions` + RenderExecutePrompt tail, execute.go:471-477): verifiable evidence or explicit safe diagnostic required; `[/]` + `— Deferred: ` protocol; never mark deferred work complete. # Context Pack: `sprint-execute-resume` — Sprint execute queue and resume

Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen, clean tree).
Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
Domain: governed-sprint-delivery. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.

## 1. Purpose

Executes the top-level task checkboxes of a validated `plan.md` through a reusable agent session, with product-owned durability around every agent turn:

- **Queue execution**: one ordered pass over plan tasks; first turn gets shared sprint context + full queue; later turns are compact continuations in the same session when a reusable session ID exists (fallback: independent full prompts).
- **Persist-before-launch checkpointing**: each task is persisted as `running` before the runtime call, and its terminal outcome is persisted before the next task starts; session IDs observed mid-stream are also checkpointed.
- **Stop-on-failure discipline**: queue halts on the first failed or cancelled task.
- **Stale-running reconcile**: `running` records left by dead owners become `failed` with diagnostics at three distinct points (startup recovery, resume reconciliation, pre-execution check).
- **Deferral protocol**: CLI `--defer --reason` (operator) or an agent-authored plan marker `- [/] Task N: ... — Deferred: <reason>` (agent); both require rationale and produce durable `deferred` outcomes; the plan checkbox stays visibly unchecked.
- **Resume validation**: `--resume` allows checked/deferred plan markers only when the run state already records matching terminal outcomes per stable task ID.
- **Containment**: the agent's working directory is set to the resolved approved target (worktree preferred), with in-prompt safety constraints forbidding git mutation and out-of-scope artifacts.
- **Publication**: when every task resolves (complete|deferred), git publication commits the implementation worktree (`All=true`) then the workspace artifacts (`execute.md`, `.run-state.json`), config-gated.

Primary code: `internal/sprint/execute.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_state.go`, `execute_target.go`, `execute_model.go`, plus `internal/sprint/publication.go:57-78` and `internal/app/git_publication.go`.

183: 	executionQueue := executeQueueFromState(state.Tasks, tasks, req.TaskID)
184: 	batchSessionID := ""
185: 	batchSessionModel := selection.Model
186: 	if req.Resume && filepath.Clean(state.Target.Path) == filepath.Clean(target.Path) {
187: 		if len(executionQueue) > 0 {
188: 			if first := taskByID(tasks, executionQueue[0].ID); first.ID != "" {
189: 				batchSessionModel = executeSelectionForTask(selection, first).Model
190: 			}
191: 		}
192: 		batchSessionID = reusableExecuteSession(state.Tasks, req.TaskID, batchSessionModel)
193: 	}
194: 	executionTurn := 0
195: 	for i := range state.Tasks {
196: 		task := &state.Tasks[i]
197: 		if req.TaskID != "" && task.ID != req.TaskID {
198: 			continue
199: 		}
200: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskComplete {
201: 			continue
202: 		}
203: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskRunning {
204: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
205: 			task.CompletedAt = ptrTime(now)
206: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "stale-running", Message: "recovered stale running task before resume", At: now})
207: 		}
208: 		if task.Status != ExecuteTaskPending && task.Status != ExecuteTaskFailed && task.Status != ExecuteTaskCancelled {
209: 			continue
210: 		}
211: 		start := s.now().UTC()
212: 		task.Status = ExecuteTaskRunning
213: 		task.Attempts++
214: 		task.StartedAt = &start
215: 		task.UpdatedAt = start
216: 		if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
217: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist running execute task %q: %w", task.ID, err)
218: 		}
219: 		planTask := taskByID(tasks, task.ID)
220: 		taskSelection := executeSelectionForTask(selection, planTask)
221: 		executionTurn++
222: 		continueSession := batchSessionID != "" && batchSessionModel == taskSelection.Model
223: 		stagePrompt := ""
224: 		promptPrefix := sharedPrefix
225: 		if continueSession {
226: 			stagePrompt = RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt(sp, planTask)
227: 			promptPrefix = ""
228: 		} else {
229: 			stagePrompt = s.renderExecuteSessionPrompt(sp, planTask, executionQueue, target, taskSelection)
230: 		}
231: 		composedPrompt, composeErr := composeStagePromptChecked(promptPrefix, stagePrompt)
232: 		if composeErr != nil {
233: 			return result, composeErr
234: 		}
235: 		sessionMode := "initial"
236: 		if continueSession {
237: 			sessionMode = "continue"
238: 		} else if executionTurn > 1 {
239: 			sessionMode = "fresh-fallback"
240: 		}
241: 		runtimeReq := s.runtimeRequest(composedPrompt, map[string]string{
242: 			"project": sp.Project, "sprint": sp.Slug, "stage": string(StageExecute), "task": task.ID, "model_source": taskSelection.Source,
243: 			"execution_session_mode": sessionMode, "execution_turn": fmt.Sprintf("%d", executionTurn), "execution_queue_size": fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(executionQueue)),
244: 		})
245: 		runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path
246: 		if continueSession {
247: 			runtimeReq.SessionID = batchSessionID
248: 			runtimeReq.SessionAction = "continue"
249: 		}
250: 		previousOnEvent := runtimeReq.OnEvent
251: 		var sessionMu sync.Mutex
252: 		var sessionSaveErr error
253: 		runtimeReq.OnEvent = func(event pruntime.Event) {
254: 			if previousOnEvent != nil {
255: 				previousOnEvent(event)
256: 			}
257: 			sessionMu.Lock()
258: 			defer sessionMu.Unlock()
259: 			if event.SessionID == "" || (task.Runtime != nil && task.Runtime.SessionID == event.SessionID) {
260: 				return
261: 			}
262: 			task.Runtime = &ExecuteRuntimeSummary{SessionID: event.SessionID, Model: taskSelection.Model, ModelSource: taskSelection.Source, OmissionReason: "raw runtime payloads omitted"}
263: 			task.UpdatedAt = s.now().UTC()
264: 			state.UpdatedAt = task.UpdatedAt
265: 			if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil && sessionSaveErr == nil {
266: 				sessionSaveErr = err
267: 			}
268: 		}
269: 		run, runErr := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, StageExecute, runtimeReq)
270: 		sessionMu.Lock()
271: 		checkpointErr := sessionSaveErr
272: 		sessionMu.Unlock()
273: 		result.Runtime = append(result.Runtime, run)
274: 		finish := s.now().UTC()
275: 		task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(task.Runtime, runtimeSummary(run, taskSelection))
276: 		if runErr == nil {
277: 			batchSessionID = run.SessionID
278: 			batchSessionModel = taskSelection.Model
279: 			if batchSessionID == "" && task.Runtime != nil {
280: 				batchSessionID = task.Runtime.SessionID
281: 			}
282: 		}
283: 		task.UpdatedAt = finish
284: 		task.CompletedAt = &finish
285: 		deferReason, deferErr := s.agentDeferredTaskReason(sp, task.ID)
286: 		switch {
287: 		case checkpointErr != nil:
288: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
289: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "state-save-failed", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.state_save_error", checkpointErr.Error()), At: finish})
290: 		case deferErr != nil:
291: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
292: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "invalid-deferral", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.defer_error", deferErr.Error()), At: finish})
293: 		case deferReason != "":
294: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskDeferred
295: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "deferred", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.defer_reason", deferReason), At: finish})
296: 		case ctx.Err() != nil:
297: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskCancelled
298: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "cancelled", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.cancelled", ctx.Err().Error()), At: finish})
299: 		case runErr != nil:
300: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
301: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "runtime-failed", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.runtime_error", safeError(runErr)), At: finish})
302: 		case len(run.Artifacts) > 0:
303: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskComplete
304: 			for _, artifact := range run.Artifacts {
305: 				task.Evidence = append(task.Evidence, ExecuteEvidence{Kind: artifact.Kind, Summary: safeExecuteText("execute.evidence", firstNonEmptyString(artifact.Description, artifact.ID)), Path: safeArtifactPath(artifact.URI)})
306: 			}
307: 		case hasDiagnosticOnlyCompletion(run):
308: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskComplete
309: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "diagnostic-only-completion", Message: "runtime reported safe diagnostic-only completion", At: finish})
310: 		default:
311: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
312: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "missing-evidence", Message: "runtime succeeded without expected evidence", At: finish})
313: 		}
314: 		if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
315: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal execute task %q: %w", task.ID, err)
316: 		}
317: 		if checkpointErr != nil {
318: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist runtime session for execute task %q: %w", task.ID, checkpointErr)
319: 		}
320: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskFailed || task.Status == ExecuteTaskCancelled {
321: 			break
322: 		}
323: 		if req.TaskID != "" {
324: 			break
325: 		}
326: 	}
327: 	if err := WriteExecuteSummary(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
328: 		return result, err
329: 	}
330: 	statePath, _ := ExecuteRunStatePath(s.root, sp)
331: 	result.RunStatePath = workspace.Rel(s.root, statePath)
332: 	result.SummaryPath = ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute)
333: 	result.Tasks = state.Tasks
334: 	result.Message = executeResultMessage(state.Tasks)
335: 	if hasFailedExecuteTask(state.Tasks) {
336: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("execute completed with failed tasks")
337: 	}
338: 	for _, run := range result.Runtime {
339: 		_ = s.deleteCompletedSessions(ctx, run)
340: 	}
341: 	if allExecuteTasksResolved(state.Tasks) {
342: 		publications, publishErr := s.publishExecuteStage(ctx, sp, target)
343: 		result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
344: 		if publishErr != nil {
345: 			return result, publishErr
346: 		}
347: 	}
348: 	return result, nil
349: }

351: func (s Service) prepareExecute(projectRef, sprintRef string, req ExecuteRequest) (Sprint, []ExecutePlanTask, ExecuteTargetRef, ExecuteModelSelection, []ValidationFinding, error) {
352: 	sp, inputs, catalog, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
353: 	if err != nil {
354: 		return Sprint{}, nil, ExecuteTargetRef{}, ExecuteModelSelection{}, nil, err
355: 	}
356: 	manifest, findings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
357: 	var target ExecuteTargetRef
358: 	if len(findings) == 0 {
359: 		var targetFindings []ValidationFinding
360: 		target, targetFindings = s.resolveSprintTarget(sp, inputs.ProjectIndex, false)
361: 		findings = append(findings, targetFindings...)
362: 	}
363: 	var tasks []ExecutePlanTask
364: 	if len(findings) == 0 {
365: 		data, readErr := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StagePlan)
366: 		if readErr != nil {
367: 			findings = append(findings, finding("plan.md", "", ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "missing plan", readErr.Error(), "Generate and validate plan.md before execute."))
368: 		} else {
369: 			tasks, findings = extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, req.Resume)
370: 			if req.Resume && len(findings) == 0 {
371: 				findings = append(findings, s.validateResolvedResumeTasks(sp, tasks, manifest.OutputPath)...)
372: 			}
373: 		}
374: 	}
375: 	if req.TaskID != "" && len(findings) == 0 && taskByID(tasks, req.TaskID).ID == "" {
376: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", req.TaskID, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "unknown execute task", "selected task id does not exist in plan.md", "Use a task id from validate execute or run without --task."))
377: 	}
378: 	selection := s.executeModelSelection(req.ModelOverride)
379: 	if selection.Model == "" {
380: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Configuration", "execute model", "", "missing execute model", "no execute model configured", "Set planning.execute_model, planning.plan_model, models.primary, or models.default."))
381: 	}
382: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
383: 	return sp, tasks, target, selection, findings, nil
384: }

386: func (s Service) validateResolvedResumeTasks(sp Sprint, tasks []ExecutePlanTask, planPath string) []ValidationFinding {
387: 	var resolved []ExecutePlanTask
388: 	for _, task := range tasks {
389: 		if task.Checked || task.Deferred {
390: 			resolved = append(resolved, task)
391: 		}
392: 	}
393: 	if len(resolved) == 0 {
394: 		return nil
395: 	}
396: 	state, err := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp)
397: 	if err != nil {
398: 		return []ValidationFinding{finding("Tasks", "", planPath, "checked tasks lack execution state", "one or more top-level tasks are checked but no valid resumable execution state exists", "Restore the matching .run-state.json or leave tasks unchecked for a new execution.")}
399: 	}
400: 	byID := make(map[string]ExecuteTaskStatus, len(state.Tasks))
401: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
402: 		byID[task.ID] = task.Status
403: 	}
404: 	var findings []ValidationFinding
405: 	for _, task := range resolved {
406: 		expected := ExecuteTaskComplete
407: 		problem := "checked task is not complete in execution state"
408: 		detail := "top-level task is checked without a matching complete run-state record"
409: 		suggestion := "Restore the task checkbox to unchecked or reconcile the execution state before resuming."
410: 		if task.Deferred {
411: 			expected = ExecuteTaskDeferred
412: 			problem = "plan deferral is not recorded in execution state"
413: 			detail = "top-level task uses [/] without a matching deferred run-state record"
414: 			suggestion = "Resume the owning execute attempt so it can record the deferral, or restore the task marker to unchecked."
415: 		}
416: 		if byID[task.ID] != expected {
417: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", task.Name, planPath, problem, detail, suggestion))
418: 		}
419: 	}
420: 	return findings
421: }

423: func (s Service) agentDeferredTaskReason(sp Sprint, taskID string) (string, error) {
424: 	data, err := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StagePlan)
425: 	if err != nil {
426: 		return "", err
427: 	}
428: 	inputs, err := s.store.ReadPlanningInputs(sp)
429: 	if err != nil {
430: 		return "", err
431: 	}
432: 	catalog, parseFindings := project.ParseProjectIndex(inputs.ProjectIndex)
433: 	if len(parseFindings) > 0 {
434: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("project-index.md has malformed catalog rows")
435: 	}
436: 	manifest, findings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
437: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
438: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("plan manifest is invalid")
439: 	}
440: 	tasks, findings := extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, true)
441: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
442: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("plan changed to an invalid task state")
443: 	}
444: 	for _, task := range tasks {
445: 		if task.ID == taskID && task.Deferred {
446: 			return task.DeferReason, nil
447: 		}
448: 	}
449: 	return "", nil
450: }

519: func renderExecuteQueue(currentTaskID string, queue []ExecutePlanTask) string {

547: func executeQueueFromState(records []ExecuteTaskRecord, tasks []ExecutePlanTask, taskID string) []ExecutePlanTask {
548: 	queue := make([]ExecutePlanTask, 0, len(records))
549: 	for _, record := range records {
550: 		if taskID != "" && record.ID != taskID {
551: 			continue
552: 		}
553: 		if record.Status == ExecuteTaskComplete || record.Status == ExecuteTaskDeferred {
554: 			continue
555: 		}
556: 		if task := taskByID(tasks, record.ID); task.ID != "" {
557: 			queue = append(queue, task)
558: 		}
559: 	}
560: 	return queue
561: }

620: func reconcileExecuteState(existing ExecuteRunState, planned []ExecuteTaskRecord, now time.Time) ExecuteRunState {
621: 	byID := map[string]ExecuteTaskRecord{}
622: 	for _, task := range existing.Tasks {
623: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskRunning {
624: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
625: 			task.CompletedAt = &now
626: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "stale-running", Message: "recovered stale running task on resume", At: now})
627: 		}
628: 		byID[task.ID] = task
629: 	}
630: 	for i, task := range planned {
631: 		if old, ok := byID[task.ID]; ok {
632: 			planned[i] = old
633: 		}
634: 	}
635: 	existing.Tasks = planned
636: 	existing.UpdatedAt = now
637: 	return existing
638: }

644: func formatRuntimeUsage(usage pruntime.Usage) string {
645: 	var parts []string
646: 	appendKnown := func(name string, known bool, value int64) {
647: 		if known {
648: 			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s=%d", name, value))
649: 		}
650: 	}
651: 	appendKnown("input", usage.InputTokensKnown, usage.InputTokens)
652: 	appendKnown("output", usage.OutputTokensKnown, usage.OutputTokens)
653: 	appendKnown("reasoning", usage.ReasoningTokensKnown, usage.ReasoningTokens)
654: 	appendKnown("cache_read", usage.CacheReadTokensKnown, usage.CacheReadTokens)

Notes on execute_state.go:

1. `safeRelPath`: checks clean != "." and no "../" prefix. But what about a path like "foo/../../etc"? filepath.Clean("foo/../../etc") = "../etc" → prefix ../ → rejected. Good. What about "..a/b"? Clean keeps "..a/b" — not a traversal. OK. Windows backslashes? ToSlash on linux. `\x00` checked. What about paths with "\r\n"? Not checked for evidence.Path... evidence Path with newline — safeRelPath doesn't check \r\n. Hmm, minor. Evidence path written into JSON (escaped) and summary. Not a real issue.

2. `SaveExecuteRunState` when DB-authoritative: writes DB first, then file only at checkpoint. Note: **when DB mode is on and checkpoint happens, the file is saved; but between DB save and file save, if the process crashes, DB and file diverge** — Load prefers DB. Fine.

3. Interesting: In DB mode, non-terminal saves return nil after DB write — meaning `.run-state.json` on disk may be stale/absent during execution. Resume validation (`validateResolvedResumeTasks`) calls LoadExecuteRunState which prefers DB. Consistent.

4. `saveExecuteRunStateWithHooks` sets `state.UpdatedAt = time.Now().UTC()` unconditionally — overwrites caller's UpdatedAt. Fine.

138: 	if err != nil {
139: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("target is not a Git worktree: %w", err)
140: 	}
141: 	root = filepath.Clean(root)
142: 	if filepath.Clean(source) != root {
143: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("target must be the Git worktree root %q", root)
144: 	}
145: 	dirty, err := gitOutput(source, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=normal")
146: 	if err != nil {

148: 	}

151: 	}

Notes on execute_plan.go:

1. `parseTopLevelTaskLine`: `trimmed[5:]` — assumes prefix "- [x]" or "- [/]" is exactly 5 chars. `isTopLevelTaskCheckbox` — need to see it. If line is `- [X] Task 1: ...` (uppercase X), ToLower prefix check works, trimmed[5:] fine (ASCII). What about `- [x]` with trailing spaces before ]? Not matched. OK.

2. `deferredTaskReason(line)`: `strings.TrimSpace(line)[5:]` — potential panic if line shorter than 5 chars? Called only when isDeferredTaskLine true → prefix "- [/" → len ≥ 5. OK.

3. **Stable ID excludes Checked/Deferred/Model** — test-asserted. ID = hash(name + decisions + requirements + evidence) normalized. Note: evidence list derived heuristically from steps containing "test"/"check"/"evidence"/"verification" substrings. So editing a step to add the word "check" changes Evidence → changes task ID! That means mid-sprint plan edits that touch steps can silently re-ID tasks and orphan prior records on resume. Documented ("renamed/edited tasks get new IDs"). By design.

4. `splitDeferredTaskReason` regex: `\s+(?:—|-)\s+deferred:\s*(.+?)\s*$` — case-insensitive. Note: a task name containing " - deferred:" would be split. Also note the em-dash OR hyphen. A deferral reason itself could contain " - deferred: ..." — only first match used (FindStringSubmatchIndex finds leftmost). Fine.

5. **`parseTopLevelTaskLine` strips model annotation BEFORE deferred-reason split? No — order: body = trimmed[5:], then splitDeferredTaskReason(body), then model annotation extraction from body (which already had deferred reason removed). Wait: `body, _ = splitDeferredTaskReason(body)` removes the deferred suffix; then model annotation extracted from remaining body. Then FindStringSubmatchIndex on body "Task 1: Name" → no model. Hmm so model annotation placed after the deferred reason is ignored for model but included in reason text. Model annotation charset restricted anyway. Minor.

6. **`extractExecutePlanTasks` returns findings for checked tasks when !allowChecked — but ALSO still builds tasks list... no wait: findings non-empty → return nil at line 112-115. Good — fail closed.

reasoning_details.text:
Interesting: `runtimeRequest` sets `req.WorkDir = s.root` (workspace root) by default, and execute overrides to target.Path. Also note at line 1166-1181: for stage metadata, if `s.runtimeForStage(stage)` has a Model override, it splits and sets req.Provider/req.Model. So the runtime request's model is set from stageRuntime — which matches executeModelSelection's source. But wait: for a task with inline annotation, `taskSelection` differs from batch selection. Does runtimeRequest override the model with stageRuntime model even when the task has an annotation? Let me check: in Execute loop, `runtimeReq := s.runtimeRequest(composedPrompt, map[...]{... "model_source": taskSelection.Source ...})`. Inside runtimeRequest, line 1172-1175: `if override, ok := s.runtimeForStage(stage); ok { if override.Model != "" { req.Provider, req.Model = splitProviderModel(override.Model) } }`.

So if planning.execute_model is configured (stageRuntime[StageExecute].Model != ""), EVERY task's runtime request gets Provider/Model from planning.execute_model REGARDLESS of the inline plan annotation! But `taskSelection` says "plan.md task annotation" and metadata model_source claims the annotation. The actual model used would be the configured one, not the annotated one!

Wait — need to check `s.stageRuntime` vs `runtimeForStage`. Let me look. And check whether runtimeConfig.Provider/Model defaults are set. req starts as s.runtimeConfig (which has Provider/Model). Then stage override replaces them.

So there are two candidate bugs:
A) Inline plan-annotated model is NOT actually applied to the runtime request when planning.execute_model (or plan model / stage runtime) is set — the request model is overridden by the stage runtime config inside runtimeRequest. The selection/metadata claim the annotation wins ("model_source": "plan.md task annotation"), but the wire-level model is the stage default. That's an error-truth/observability defect: state records RuntimeSummary.Model = annotated model while actual run used different model. Need to verify how startSprintRuntime uses req.Provider/req.Model vs selection.

B) Even without annotations: executeModelSelection precedence (override > execute_model > plan_model > provider/model) vs runtimeRequest's stage override — consistent for execute stage since both use stageRuntime[StageExecute].

Let me verify runtimeForStage and stageRuntime construction, and whether ModelOverride (command --model) reaches the runtime request. executeModelSelection(override) returns selection with Source "command override". But does the runtime REQUEST get the override model? In Execute loop, runtimeReq comes from s.runtimeRequest which sets req.Provider/Model from s.runtimeConfig then possibly stage override. The command override (`--model`) is only in `selection`, used for prompts/metadata/reuse gating, but NOT applied to req.Provider/req.Model unless stageRuntime reflects it!

Wait — in app wiring, sprintRuntimeService may rebuild service with stage runtime models where execute stage model = override? Let me check internal/app/sprint_commands.go around 685-711.

So `sprintRuntimeService` builds the service WITHOUT any `--model` override applied to stageRuntime. The CLI `--model` flag sets `req.ModelOverride` in ExecuteRequest, used only via `executeModelSelection(override)` → selection. But `runtimeRequest` sets `req.Provider, req.Model = splitProviderModel(override.Model)` from `s.runtimeForStage(stage)` — the stage runtime map, which contains planning.execute_model etc., NOT the command override. So: **`ultraplan sprint

execute --model provider/model`** — does the actual runtime call use the overridden model? Let me check `RequestFromConfig` and how startSprintRuntime passes Provider/Model, plus where ModelOverride is honored elsewhere (flow? review?). Let me check Review to compare — review.go probably applies ModelOverride differently. Also check `startSprintRuntime` in runtime_metrics.go.

reasoning_details.text:
Review explicitly overrides `req.Model` from the manifest model (line 902). Execute does NOT — it relies on `runtimeRequest`'s internal stage override, which never sees the command `--model` override or the per-task plan annotation.

So candidate defect #1 (strong): **Execute's `--model` flag and inline plan `<!-- model: ... -->` annotations do not reach the runtime request.** The selection (and thus prompts, metadata `model_source`, run-state RuntimeSummary.Model/ModelSource, session-reuse gating) claims the annotated/overridden model, but the actual runtime request uses whatever `runtimeRequest` computed from config/stageRuntime. Evidence:
- execute.go:241-245: runtimeReq built via s.runtimeRequest with metadata only; no Provider/Model adjustment.
- service.go:1166-1181: only stageRuntime override applied.
- code_context.go:293-294 and review.go:902 show the established pattern of applying override to request — absent in execute.

Consequences:
1. `--model openai/gpt-x` silently runs planning.execute_model/config default → wrong model executes tasks; operator believes override honored.
2. Plan annotation `<!-- model: provider/model -->` documented as overriding per-task model (test asserts executeSelectionForTask precedence; prompt prints "Model source: plan.md task annotation") but actual run uses configured model.
3. Session-reuse gating compares taskSelection.Model against record.Runtime.Model (which is derived from the fake selection) — consistent within its own fiction, so reuse works, but the recorded model is wrong vs actual.
4. Metrics (.runtime-metrics.json) record req.Model = actual requested model → state file says one thing, metrics another; observable inconsistency proving the mismatch.

Wait — need to double check: maybe runtimeConfig.Provider/Model are empty and the adapter reads model from... no, RequestFromConfig(effective.Config, root.Path). Let me check RequestFromConfig to see what sets Provider/Model defaults. Also check whether startSprintRuntime's controlled runtime wrapper injects model from metadata? Let me check controlledRuntimeFor and platform/runtime StartRun to see which fields drive the actual model call.

Runs or previews the governed stage flow through smoke. Cumulative planning order is `requirements -> code-context -> sprint-index -> technical-handbook -> area-reasoning -> reasoning -> plan`; `flow --to plan` dispatches code-context exactly once when it is not already complete and valid. A code-context rerun reads the configured implementation target with restricted permissions and atomically replaces only `code-context.md`. A non-dry-run flow reports each stage as it is checked, started, skipped, completed, or failed and interleaves sanitized runtime progress. Review and smoke use the same sprint-owned transition as `verify`. Compatible interrupted reviews resume by default; `--restart-review` discards retained review progress. A non-dry-run smoke transition requires `--yes`.

### `ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> execute`

```text
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> execute [--task <id>] [--dry-run] [--resume] [--model <provider/model>]
```

Executes validated top-level `plan.md` task checkboxes through one reusable generic-runtime agent session. The first turn receives the shared sprint context, ordered queue, and current task; each later task is a compact continuation in that session. UltraPlan checkpoints each task before advancing, stops the queue on failure/cancellation, writes `.run-state.json` and `execute.md`, requires runtime evidence or a safe diagnostic before marking a task complete, and constrains work to the project index target implementation directory. If the runtime supplies no reusable session ID, execution safely falls back to complete independent prompts.

Explicitly defer accepted follow-up work with a required rationale:

```text
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> execute --task <id> --defer --reason "accepted rationale and follow-up owner"
```

Deferral is a durable terminal outcome shown in `execute.md` and status counts. The plan checkbox remains unchecked so deferred work is not represented as implemented. Review accepts it only when the unchecked task's stable ID has a matching governed `deferred` outcome; arbitrary unchecked or manually checked tasks cannot bypass execution.

The normal agent-owned path uses the plan itself. During an active execute attempt, the execute agent may replace the task's top-level `[ ]` marker with `[/]` and append an inline rationale:

```markdown
- [/] **Task 6: Persist shutdown uncertainty** — Deferred: requires a separately governed owner capability in Sprint 32
```

After the runtime returns, UltraPlan validates the reason, preserves the task's stable ID, records the durable `deferred` outcome, and continues with the next task. A `[/]` marker without `— Deferred: <reason>` is invalid. A pre-existing marker cannot bypass a new execution or review unless the matching run-state already records that deferral.

A code-context rerun reads the configured implementation target with restricted permissions and atomically replaces only `code-context.md`. A non-dry-run flow reports each stage as it is checked, started, skipped, completed, or failed and interleaves sanitized runtime progress. Review and smoke use the same sprint-owned transition as `verify`. Compatible interrupted reviews resume by default; `--restart-review` discards retained review progress. A non-dry-run smoke transition requires `--yes`.

### `ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> execute`

```text
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> execute [--task <id>] [--dry-run] [--resume] [--model <provider/model>]
```

Executes validated top-level `plan.md` task checkboxes through one reusable generic-runtime agent session. The first turn receives the shared sprint context, ordered queue, and current task; each later task is a compact continuation in that session. UltraPlan checkpoints each task before advancing, stops the queue on failure/cancellation, writes `.run-state.json` and `execute.md`, requires runtime evidence or a safe diagnostic before marking a task complete, and constrains work to the project index target implementation directory. If the runtime supplies no reusable session ID, execution safely falls back to complete independent prompts.

Explicitly defer accepted follow-up work with a required rationale:

```text
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> execute --task <id> --defer --reason "accepted rationale and follow-up owner"
```

Deferral is a durable terminal outcome shown in `execute.md` and status counts. The plan checkbox remains unchecked so deferred work is not represented as implemented. Review accepts it only when the unchecked task's stable ID has a matching governed `deferred` outcome; arbitrary unchecked or manually checked tasks cannot bypass execution.

The normal agent-owned path uses the plan itself. During an active execute attempt, the execute agent may replace the task's top-level `[ ]` marker with `[/]` and append an inline rationale:

```markdown
- [/] **Task 6: Persist shutdown uncertainty** — Deferred: requires a separately governed owner capability in Sprint 32
```

After the runtime returns, UltraPlan validates the reason, preserves the task's stable ID, records the durable `deferred` outcome, and continues with the next task. A `[/]` marker without `— Deferred: <reason>` is invalid. A pre-existing marker cannot bypass a new execution or review unless the matching run-state already records that deferral.

reasoning_details.text:
**CONFIRMED — Finding 2 (data race / state corruption):** In `Adapter.StartRun`, events are pumped by a background goroutine (`go func() { for event := range run.Events() { ... req.OnEvent(mapped) } }()`), and `StartRun` returns as soon as `run.Wait` completes — it does NOT wait for the events goroutine to drain (only up to 1 second for `eventsCh`, then proceeds; on timeout the goroutine keeps running). So `req.OnEvent` (the execute checkpoint closure) can be invoked CONCURRENTLY WITH and AFTER `startSprintRuntime` returns, while the main Execute loop mutates `task.Status/Attempts/Diagnostics/Evidence/Runtime/UpdatedAt` and `state.UpdatedAt` WITHOUT holding `sessionMu`.

The execute code (execute.go:250-272) guards only `sessionSaveErr` with `sessionMu`; the closure itself writes `task.Runtime`, `task.UpdatedAt`, `state.UpdatedAt` and calls `SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state)` reading the WHOLE `state` struct concurrently with main-loop writes. Two concrete failure modes:

a) Go data race (unsynchronized concurrent read/write of task fields, state.Tasks slice header unchanged but element fields written concurrently) — undefined behavior, `-race` would flag.

b) Torn persisted snapshots: OnEvent's SaveExecuteRunState can serialize a mid-mutation state (e.g., task.Status=running while CompletedAt already set, or terminal status persisted without evidence yet appended... wait order: classification happens after run returns; events may still be arriving). Worse: after terminal save at line 314, a straggler event could checkpoint task.Runtime + SaveExecuteRunState AGAIN, re-writing the file AFTER the terminal save — potentially persisting a state where UpdatedAt moved backwards? No, it sets UpdatedAt=now. But consider: event arrives during line 314-319 window; both saves race → last-writer-wins with mixed field versions. Also validation could fail transiently: e.g., main sets Status=complete (terminal requires CompletedAt non-nil — set at 284 before classification), fine. But mid-window: main loop at 212-215 sets Status=running/StartedAt while OnEvent marshal reads → JSON marshal of concurrently-mutating structs is itself a race (map/slice iteration).

Also note: the same race exists in review.go's runReviewer OnEvent? There OnEvent only calls captured.observe(event.Payload) + onSession(sessionID) — reviewOutputCapture presumably has own mutex; onSession updates review session tracking... different surface.

For execute specifically: is there any synchronization ensuring events are drained before return? Line 385-401: `select { case events := <-eventsCh: ... case <-time.After(time.Second): }`. After Wait() returns, typically events channel closes quickly, BUT if the agent emitted many events or the stream stalls, StartRun returns after ≤1s leaving the pump running. Then Execute continues mutating state while OnEvent may still fire. Even in the common case, between `run.Wait` completion and events-drain completion there IS a window where OnEvent fires concurrently with post-`StartRun` main-loop code (line 270+ executes immediately when StartRun returns, not waiting for eventsCh).

Actually wait — even MORE important: the 1-second timeout path means mapped.Events may be nil and SessionIDs empty, while OnEvent keeps getting called afterwards. The main loop at line 275 `task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(task.Runtime, runtimeSummary(run, taskSelection))` runs concurrently with an OnEvent invocation writing `task.Runtime = &ExecuteRuntimeSummary{...}` → lost update/race.

Is this reachable in production? The opencode adapter's run.Events(): need to confirm events actually stream asynchronously (not all delivered synchronously before Wait returns). The architecture (channel + separate goroutine + Wait) strongly implies async streaming. Let me check the agentwrap opencode adapter briefly for Events() semantics.

part.text: The runtime pumps events on a background goroutine that can outlive `StartRun`. Probing whether execute's checkpoint closure races with the post-run main loop.

reasoning_details.text:
Confirmed the adapter's `run.Events()` is an async channel (buffered 32) fed by a goroutine scanning stdout; `close(r.events)` happens when `run()` finishes. `run.Wait()` presumably waits for `r.done` — which is closed in the SAME deferred sequence as close(r.events): `defer close(r.events); defer close(r.done)` — defers run LIFO: close(r.done) runs FIRST, then close(r.events). So when Wait returns, events channel may not yet be closed/drained! And in platform/runtime Adapter.StartRun, after Wait returns there's only up to 1 second grace waiting for eventsCh (which closes AFTER the pump goroutine drains). If drain takes >1s (large event streams — long agent turns produce hundreds/thousands of events), StartRun returns while OnEvent callbacks are still firing.

So in Execute: main loop proceeds to mutate task/state and call SaveExecuteRunState concurrently with the OnEvent closure doing the same → genuine data race + potential corrupted `.run-state.json` snapshots (marshal races) and lost updates (e.g., checkpoint overwrites terminal classification? No—checkpoint only sets Runtime/UpdatedAt then saves whole state read at marshal time... json.Marshal of a struct being concurrently written = race, could persist mixed-version data).

Also even without >1s drain: between Wait() return and pump completion there IS always a window where OnEvent can fire after StartRun returns (events buffered but not drained). The window is real every turn; whether it manifests depends on timing. With `-race` in tests using fake runtimes it never triggers because fakes call OnEvent synchronously inside StartRun.

This is a solid finding: REALITY evidence = runtime.go:331-344 (pump goroutine), 385-401 (1s abandon), execute.go:250-272+275-316 (unguarded shared mutation). Bad outcome: data race (UB), torn/partial JSON snapshots of .run-state.json, lost session checkpoints, or validation failures mid-save (e.g., marshal sees Status=running with CompletedAt set — actually running requires StartedAt set — fine; but e.g. terminal status with CompletedAt visible before Diagnostics append? appends happen before save in main; interleaving could marshal Status=failed-without-completedAt? CompletedAt set at 284 BEFORE status assignment at 287+. Hmm: line 283-284 set UpdatedAt/CompletedAt first, then switch sets Status. An OnEvent save racing between those sees old Status=pending/running with CompletedAt non-nil — pending isn't terminal so no completedAt requirement; running requires StartedAt (set). Deferred requires rationale — not yet appended if status set to deferred but diagnostic append happens atomically within same case... In the deferred case: Status=ExecuteTaskDeferred assigned at 294, diagnostics appended 295 — a checkpoint save between those two lines (single-threaded main can't be preempted mid-case by itself, but the OTHER goroutine's SaveExecuteRunState marshals whenever it fires — it would see Status=deferred with diagnostics maybe not yet appended IF the event goroutine reads state exactly between line 294 and 295 executions. Go scheduler can preempt between those statements; OnEvent goroutine marshals → deferred task without rationale diagnostic → ValidateExecuteRunState error → checkpoint save fails → sessionSaveErr set → task classified FAILED ("state-save-failed") despite successful deferral! That's a concrete misclassification path. Low probability but real.

Race detector proof: I can write a repro with a fake runtime that mimics async event delivery (spawn goroutine emitting events after returning result). Let me do that in the scratch copy.

Also note the same unguarded pattern applies to `state` being saved by OnEvent while main-loop holds NO lock — plus SaveExecuteRunState from two goroutines concurrently: atomicWriteFile uses CreateTemp+rename — concurrent saves don't corrupt file (rename atomic), but content can interleave versions. The primary hazard is the unsynchronized struct access.

Let me write the race repro now.

reasoning_details.text:
Web mapping fine. Now let me do a final check on a few remaining hypotheses:

1. **`agentDeferredTaskReason` uses `extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, true)`** — allowChecked=true. If agent checked the task `[x]` instead of deferring (misbehaving agent), Deferred=false → returns "" → classification falls through to artifacts/complete — and the CHECKED marker in plan.md now disagrees with state... but validateResolvedResumeTasks on a LATER resume would catch `[x]` without complete record? If the task completed with artifacts, state=complete matches [x] → consistent. If task failed but agent checked it: state=failed; later resume → finding "checked tasks lack execution state"... actually mismatch → blocked with actionable message. Fail-closed. Good.

2. **`extractExecutePlanTasks` in `agentDeferredTaskReason` runs with allowChecked=true — if plan became invalid (syntax error), deferErr set → "invalid-deferral" failed. Good.

3. **`DeferExecuteTask` doesn't update execute.md counts for evidence? WriteExecuteSummary(state) — yes regenerates.

4. **`Execute` result.Findings returned when prepareExecute findings — renderSprintExecute prints them; ExitValidation. Good.

5. One more potential correctness item: **`executeQueueFromState` excludes records whose status is complete/deferred, but includes FAILED records — queue order = planned order filtered. Continuation prompt lists queue INCLUDING current task marked "current". Fine.

6. **Attempts counting**: stale-running→failed→immediately re-executed in same resume run: Attempts++ once per launch. Validation requires attempts≥0 only. OK.

7. **`task.Runtime` checkpoint during events then `mergeRuntimeSummary(task.Runtime, runtimeSummary(run,...))`: runtimeSummary sets SessionID=run.SessionID; if empty, keeps previous (event-observed). Model fields from selection (Finding 1 taint). OmissionReason preserved from event-set summary? mergeRuntimeSummary returns CURRENT summary with SessionID backfilled — losing OmissionReason/Model from event summary but those equal selection anyway. Fine.

8. Let me quickly verify the **`safeError` truncation 180 chars** exists as claimed (not critical).

9. **`renderSprintExecute` per-task lines show diagnostics — good observability.

I think I have my finding set. Let me also spot-check one more potential real bug in extraction: **bold-tolerant parsing `- [ ] **Task 1: Name**`**: parseTopLevelTaskLine: body after checkbox = "**Task 1: Name**"; splitDeferredTaskReason no-op; model none; body=strings.Trim(body,"* ") → "Task 1: Name"; regex ^Task\s+\d+\s*: matches; return body trimmed again. But Trim(body,"* ") also strips leading/trailing asterisks AND spaces anywhere at edges — name ending with "*" loses it. Cosmetic.

**Task names containing em-dash deferred-like text**: `- [ ] Task 1: Fix - deferred: nothing` → isDeferredTaskLine false ([ ]); but parseTopLevelTaskLine splits reason "nothing" OFF THE NAME → name becomes "Task 1: Fix"! And deferred flag NOT set (marker is [ ]) so task executes; DeferReason field not set either (deferredTaskReason only called for [/] lines... wait line 66-67: deferred := isDeferredTaskLine(line); deferReason := deferredTaskReason(line) — computed for ALL top-level lines but used only if deferred. For [ ] lines with " - deferred:" text in name: parseTopLevelTaskLine strips the suffix from displayed name silently. Name change → ID change vs un-stripped variant... deterministic anyway. Edge-case cosmetic.

Now — I should also double-check Finding 2's applicability to the CONTROLLED runtime wrapper: controlledRuntime.StartRun wraps base Adapter.StartRun and its own OnEvent holds eventMu while calling configuredOnEvent (the execute closure) — meaning execute's SaveExecuteRunState runs UNDER run_control's eventMu, serializing concurrent OnEvent invocations against EACH OTHER but not against main loop. Race stands (empirically proven via direct fake; production chain preserves async delivery).

One more sanity check for Finding 2 counter-evidence: does anything wait on `run.Events()` drain before returning? Adapter waits ≤1s for eventsCh AFTER Wait() returns. The pump closes eventsCh only after channel closed+drained. In the COMMON case (small remaining buffer) drain completes <1s and StartRun returns AFTER final OnEvent — race window tiny but nonzero; in slow/large cases >1s window guaranteed. Also cancellation path (ctx.Done): returns mapped WITHOUT draining at all (5s bounded cancel wait, then immediate return while pump still running!) — execute classifies cancelled and SAVES terminal state while pump may still deliver session events → checkpoint save races terminal save. That's the strongest variant: cancelled turns have the widest window. 

Also worth noting: after Execute returns entirely (function exit), straggler OnEvent goroutines could still fire SaveExecuteRunState even AFTER publication?? Events stop when process stdout closes (run() exits → close(events)) — bounded by opencode process lifetime which ends before Wait returns typically. The 1s-abandon case means pump outlives StartRun but usually not Execute. Fine—race already proven.

Let me also quickly confirm the claim "no test constructs Resume:true execute run" is accurate for app-level tests driving full CLI execute --resume. Search app tests for "execute".

reasoning_details.text:
**CONFIRMED — Finding 4:** After a successful `--task` run with remaining queue, the run (a) records `sess-1` in `.run-state.json` as the reusable session, and (b) deletes `sess-1`. A later `--resume` selects `sess-1` for continuation — a session the product itself destroyed. Downstream consequence depends on the opencode adapter/CLI: `--session sess-1 --continue` on a missing session either errors (task misclassified "runtime-failed", stop-on-failure) or silently starts a new session that receives only a compact continuation prompt with NO shared context and NO safety instructions (RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt omits both; it merely asserts they "remain in force"). Either outcome is bad. Confidence high on product-level contradiction (empirically shown); medium-high on end-to-end failure mode.

Also note the same deletion happens for flow-dispatched partial... no—flow full-queue stops only on failure which returns early. But web/TUI execute-start with task option hits same path as CLI --task.

Wait, one more consideration: is this maybe INTENTIONAL ("deleteCompletedSessions" = sessions of COMPLETED tasks are disposable because continuation isn't desired)? Counter-evidence: `reusableExecuteSession` + resume reuse gate exist precisely to continue recorded sessions across runs, and cli-reference says execution continues in one reusable session across resumes. Deleting while queue remains contradicts that contract. Also deletion is unconditional even when publication disabled. I'm confident reporting.

Now finalize findings list:

**F1 (High, high confidence): `--model` override and per-task plan model annotations never reach the runtime request.**
- execute.go:241-249 builds runtimeReq without applying taskSelection.Model; service.go:1166-1181 applies only stageRuntime config.
- Contrast: code_context.go:293-298 and review.go:902 apply override/model to the request.
- Persisted RuntimeSummary.Model/ModelSource (execute.go:262, 640-642) and prompt "Model source" line record the fictional model; .runtime-metrics.json records the real one (runtime_metrics.go:141) → contradictory audit trail.
- Empirically proven (both probes).
- Bad outcomes: operator-selected model silently ignored; per-task routing feature non-functional; state claims wrong model; session-reuse gating decisions based on wrong identities.
- Regression test: assert captured request Provider/Model equals annotated/overridden model.

**F2 (High severity reliability, high confidence): data race between async OnEvent checkpoint closure and post-run state mutation.**
- runtime.go:331-344 pump goroutine; 385-401 ≤1s abandon (and cancellation path returns without draining at all).
- execute.go:250-272 closure guarded by sessionMu only internally; main loop mutates task/state unguarded (275-316).
- Race detector output at execute.go:259 vs :275/:641 using production-shaped async pump.
- Consequences: UB; torn JSON snapshots; spurious state-save-failed misclassification (deferred-status-without-rationale transient read); lost checkpoints.
- Untestable by current suite: fakes invoke OnEvent synchronously.

**F3 (Medium-low, high confidence): reconcileExecuteState preserves stale header (Target.Path/Source, PlanFingerprint) while executing against current target.**
- execute.go:176-179, 186-193, 620-638.
- Probe: resumed run executed with WorkDir=<current target> but persisted Target.Path stayed "/somewhere/stale/old-target".
- Also permanently defeats session-reuse gate (compares stale header vs current each time) → repeated fresh-fallback prompts.
- Fingerprint never recomputed → audit field describes original plan even after plan edits + resume.

**F4 (Medium, high confidence product-level): successful mid-queue runs delete the session recorded for later reuse.**
- execute.go:337-340 deletes after ANY failure-free completion incl. single-task mode with pending tasks; state retains deleted SessionID; reusableExecuteSession returns it on resume (probe).
- Continuation prompt omits shared context/safety instructions (execute.go:224-230, RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt), so silent-fresh fallback degrades containment guidance; hard-failure variant misclassifies as runtime-failed.

**F5 (Verification gap / misleading test evidence, medium-high confidence): resume internals 0% tested contrary to sprint-23 acceptance claim.**
- Coverage: validateResolvedResumeTasks/reusableExecuteSession/reconcileExecuteState 0.0% across whole package; Resume:true only in production wiring (flow.go:241, operation_runner.go:58).
- ultraplan-workspace sprint23 requirements.md L104 claims "Unit tests cover ... resume without redoing complete tasks".
- The untested path demonstrably contains F3; F2's checkpoint interplay also unexercised on resume.

**Minor/defensible items to report briefly:**
- Cancelled-only runs exit ExitPartial via "failed tasks" substring classification (sprint_commands.go:360-364) and message "execute failed"; durable outcome=cancelled — inconsistent signals for automation.
- ExitRuntime branch unreachable for genuine runtime failures from Execute (they exit ExitPartial) — error-classification by substring is fragile.
- Flow dispatch discards Execute's Tasks/Runtime/Publications (flow.go:241-242) — `flow --to execute` output shows only "execute complete"; publications invisible in flow output.
- deleteCompletedSessions errors ignored silently (`_ =`).

Defended non-issues:
- Dry-run persists context-pack cache (persistCache=true before DryRun branch) — cache documented disposable; no dry-run write-free contract for sprint execute in cli-reference (unlike init/materialise). Not reported as defect.
- project-index target selecting wholesale commit root — documented trust boundary (pack §6); planning chain + review gates upstream; not a new finding here.
- Non-atomic execute.md write — contract requires atomicity only for .run-state.json (sprint23 L72).
- Sixth status `deferred` vs five in sprint23 L46 — superset, documented in cli-reference.
- Fresh-state overwrite when resume load fails — fail-safe design; checked-marker validation fails closed when markers present.
- gitpublish CAS/push semantics reviewed — no defect found.

One more sanity check on F5's workspace claim line number and wording, then clean up scratch files and worktrees, then write the report.
